picks.what: Woodcut in Hartmann Schedel’s Nuremberg Chronicle
picks.why: colored true view labeled Nuremberga; castle, St. Sebald and St. Lorenz labeled and recognizable

picks.what: Panorama, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Franconiae
picks.why: full panorama with the castle, St. Lorenz and St. Sebald; legend strip trimmed

picks.what: The castle seen from St. John’s Cemetery, steel engraving
picks.why: the castle, the city’s main landmark, clearly drawn; caption trimmed

picks.what: The old town from the castle hill, photograph

gaps: P2: nothing (Merian’s Topographia Franconiae plates are dated by the 1648 volume, so they fall in P1); no second P3 or P4
notes: #17: the file is from the second edition of Topographia Franconiae, dated by its first appearance in 1648 per the rules; chosen over Braun and Hogenberg’s 1575 view (#7/#11/#14), where the city is a thin strip behind large costume figures. #18 is a cropped half of the same Merian panorama. #26 (optical print of the town hall) is dated only 1742–1801 and was skipped. #22 is a later reproduction of an 1842 watercolor. #1, #3, #4, #6 are other cities or scenes from the Chronicle.
